title: How many Personal Checking accounts can one customer hold?
content:
## Scope

This policy governs the opening of a new Personal Checking account for a customer who may already hold other Personal Checking accounts as primary owner. A customer may hold several Personal Checking accounts as primary owner, subject to two caps that apply together.

## Basis of decision

1. **Overall cap.** The count of the customer's checking accounts whose status is not closed must be below **4** before a new account is opened.
2. **Tier cap.** The count of the customer's checking accounts of the requested tier whose status is not closed must be below that tier's figure for the most open accounts of the tier per customer before a new account of that tier is opened. The tier cap for each of the six tiers (Access, Student, Everyday, Interest, Premier and Private Client Checking) is that same tier's own figure for the most open accounts of the tier one customer may hold as primary owner; no tier borrows another tier's figure.
3. **What counts.** Accounts in applied, active, dormant, restricted and charged-off status all count toward both caps; closed accounts never count.
4. **Whose accounts.** Joint ownership is not modelled: an account counts only for the customer recorded on it.
5. **Outcome.** When either cap is already reached, the opening is declined and nothing is recorded.

Both caps are read from the bank's system records of the customer's checking accounts, before the account is opened; the counts concern the customer who would be the new account's primary owner and, for the tier cap, the tier being requested.

## Decision table

| Accounts not closed, all tiers | Accounts not closed, requested tier | Opening |
|---|---|---|
| Below 4 | Below the tier cap | May proceed as far as these caps are concerned |
| Below 4 | At the tier cap | Declined, nothing recorded |
| At 4 | Below the tier cap | Declined, nothing recorded |
| At 4 | At the tier cap | Declined, nothing recorded |

## Worked cases (hypothetical customers)

- **A charged-off account still counts.** A customer holds one active, one dormant and one charged-off checking account and one account closed last year. Three accounts are not closed, which is below 4, so the overall cap is not reached; the closed account is ignored.
- **The overall cap binds even when the tier cap would not.** A customer holds four accounts in active or restricted status across Everyday and Interest Checking and asks for a Premier Checking account. Four accounts are not closed, so the overall cap is reached and the opening is declined, whatever the Premier Checking tier cap.
- **An application still pending funding counts.** An account in applied status counts toward both caps just as an active one does.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "only active accounts count". **Correct basis:** every status except closed counts.
- **Wrong reading:** "a joint account held with a spouse counts for both owners". **Correct basis:** an account counts only for the customer recorded on it.
